votes.evidence:
Premise traced from render site back to the server stamping paths (all paths under /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215):

Render: tools/pr-approval-agent/reviewer.py:683-702 `_format_self_driving(self, cl)` takes only the classification dict; the sole condition is `if not cl.get("self_driving"): return ""` (line 692) and it then emits the fixed text including "It is a draft on purpose ... draft state is not a caution signal for this PR" (lines 698-700). Neither `pr.draft` nor `pr.author_is_bot` is consulted. The block is interpolated into the TRUSTED region at reviewer.py:506 and :568 (test_reviewer.py:262 asserts it sits above the untrusted delimiter).

Flag source: `cl["self_driving"] = self.self_driving` (review_pr.py:477) <- `Pipeline(..., self_driving=bool(context.get("self_driving_review")))` (review_local.py:321) <- `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451). The engine does hold `pr.draft` at render time: review_local.py:197 `draft=bool(pr.get("draft"))` from the same snapshot.

Stamping path 1 (webhook carve-out): tasks.py:870-876 runs `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` whenever `_review_skip_reason(pr)` is non-None. `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS = frozenset({"synchronize", "reopened"})` (tasks.py:49). The carve-out checks action (tasks.py:167), `_is_bot_authored` (169-172), fork safety, repo config, task-facade match and opt-in (174-215) - never `pr["draft"]`. The docstring at tasks.py:160-165 explicitly scopes it to synchronize/reopen after the initial review, and a ready_for_review flip alone is excluded. So: bot draft flips to ready -> author pushes -> `synchronize` -> `_review_skip_reason` returns "bot" (draft check no longer fires) -> carve-out stamps `inbox_review` (persisted tasks.py:1056-1064) -> the engine renders the draft sentence against a snapshot whose `draft` is False.

Stamping path 2 (receiver leg): `process_inbox_pr_review` (tasks.py:1110-1229) fetches the PR fresh and only checks `state == "open"` (tasks.py:1166-1169); no draft check before stamping `inbox_review` at tasks.py:1223-1229. Its docstring (1125-1129) says it re-fires on every TaskRun output save, so a refire after the ready flip with a new head also reaches the same stale sentence.

Impact bound: gates are unaffected (`_check_prerequisites` draft gate at review_pr.py:590 is moot for a non-draft PR), and the prompt region at reviewer.py:490-580 contains no other draft mention, so the LLM sees one false but uncontradicted statement. Fix is small: pass `pr` (or `pr.draft`) into `_format_self_driving` and drop the draft clause when `not pr.draft`.
votes.refutation:
Attempted to refute both halves of the claim.

Machine-user half: refuted. The carve-out returns empty unless `_is_bot_authored(pr)` (tasks.py:169-172), and the receiver leg is only reachable via review_hog's TaskRun receiver (`_start_stamphog_review`, products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:210) for PRs a PostHog Code implementation run opened under the team's App machine user. The engine's own `author_is_bot and not self_driving` guards (review_pr.py:225, review_local.py:324) only relax on the flag, which no human PR receives. The finding's "flag stamped on a human-authored PR" scenario has no reachable trigger.

Draft half: refutation failed. I looked for a draft guard on every hop from stamping to rendering: `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (tasks.py:144-215) has none; `process_inbox_pr_review` (tasks.py:1166-1169) checks only open state; activities.py:451 forwards the flag unconditionally; `_format_self_driving` (reviewer.py:692) keys on the flag alone. The one draft check on the path, `_review_skip_reason`, returns "draft" only while the PR is still a draft; after the ready flip the bot-author reason keeps the carve-out reachable. A bot draft made ready and then pushed is an ordinary sequence, so the stale "It is a draft on purpose" sentence in the TRUSTED block is reachable in normal operation. Severity stays at consider because the only effect is one inaccurate framing sentence in the prompt; no gate, verdict, or approval path reads it.

votes.refutation:
Attempted refutation, machine-user half: succeeds. Both stamping paths require bot authorship by construction — the webhook carve-out returns empty unless `_is_bot_authored(pr)` (tasks.py:167-170, "Self-driving PRs are always bot-authored (authorship is forced to the team's GitHub App machine user)"), and the receiver leg `process_inbox_pr_review` (tasks.py:1110-1128) is only entered from review_hog's TaskRun receiver for PostHog Code implementation runs. The engine dropping the `author_is_bot` check from its self_driving gate does not create a human-authored path to the flag. That half is speculative and not a defect.

Attempted refutation, draft half: fails. The docstring at tasks.py:160-164 only excludes the `ready_for_review` action itself; a later `synchronize` on the now-ready PR still matches (tasks.py:157) and the carve-out has no draft check. The engine's draft prerequisite (review_pr.py:590) is moot on a non-draft PR, so no gate stops the run, and the prompt text is emitted from `cl["self_driving"]` alone. No test asserts the draft sentence tracks `pr.draft`; the one prompt test asserts the opposite on a draft=False fixture.

Severity is kept at consider, not should_fix: the false sentence only affects prompt framing. Telling the reviewer "draft state is not a caution signal" on a PR that is not a draft changes no gate, no verdict path, and effectively no scrutiny (draft status was never going to be a caution signal on a ready PR). The fix is cheap (thread `pr.draft` into the render) but the blast radius is one inaccurate sentence in the trusted block on the ready-then-push path.
